transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-16
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Maria Gonzalez (Amberlane CTO), Ethan Park (Amberlane Infra), Sofia Patel (Amberlane Procurement)
Shared items: pricing sheet (link), SOC2 pack (link), benchmark template (link)

[00:00] Alex Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio ok for folks?
[00:06] Maria Gonzalez: Yep, good here.
[00:08] Ethan Park: Good.
[00:10] Alex Martinez: Awesome. So agenda — quick renewal status, go over the capacity ask for additional regions, pricing options for a 12-month extension, and then next steps — Priya will talk perf.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Hi all — I'll cover the performance/benchmark plan after Alex. Wanted to flag up front we've seen a few similar customers push dedicated across EU and APAC for latency/residency reasons.
[00:32] Maria Gonzalez: That is our primary ask — we want Amberlane's production traffic in EU and APAC handled in-region. Also looking at cost predictability; our spend has spiky peaks.
[00:40] Alex Martinez: Understood. Just to recap contract status — current hosted plan renews June 1st, and you have asked about dedicated reserved capacity across US-EAST, eu-west, and asia-southeast, plus a 12-month extension. Correct?
[00:50] Sofia Patel: Correct. Also we need procurement timelines — PO window is mid-May ideally.
[00:55] Alex Martinez: Ok. So two pieces: technical feasibility/perf and commercial. Priya, do you want to take the perf notes?
[01:02] Priya Shah: Sure. From a runtime perspective, dedicated capacity will give you much tighter tail latency and consistent throughput. For multi-region you can do one of two patterns — a dedicated pool per region or a central pool with geo-routing; for strict residency we recommend per-region pools. There's also caching considerations — prefix/KV cache stays local to the pool, so cross-region misses matter.
[01:30] Ethan Park: Quick Q — if we go dedicated per region, what's the expected cold-start behavior and how do we handle bursts? We have big month-end spikes.
[01:38] Priya Shah: Good question. Dedicated pools are warm; cold starts minimal. For spikes we can configure burst capacity — that's a buffer we price as part of the reserved commit. You can either buy higher nominal capacity or keep a smaller commit and allow bursts billed at a known uplift.
[01:56] Maria Gonzalez: What's the uplift percentage ballpark?
[01:58] Alex Martinez: Typically 15-25% on top of the reserved hourly for burst billing depending on region and GPU type. We'll show exact numbers in the quote.
[02:08] Ethan Park: OK. Also, KMS — we must keep keys in our HSM and have control of rotation. Is that supported for private keys on dedicated?
[02:16] Jordan Lee: Yes — we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations on both Dedicated and Private deployments. We'll share the integration guide and architecture notes after this call.
[02:26] Sofia Patel: Great. From procurement POV we need to see SSO/SAML, SOC2 and ISO docs, and an explicit clause about data residency for EU/UK.
[02:36] Jordan Lee: I'll attach those. SOC2 + ISO artifacts and our data residency language — we'll include them in the compliance pack.
[02:42] Maria Gonzalez: Perfect.
[02:45] Priya Shah: Back to perf — for the benchmark we'd like to run a 2-hour test that includes steady-state QPS and a 10-minute spike to simulate month-end. We'll need an API key and a test dataset; we can run with masked data. The plan is: baseline run on your current hosted config, then run on proposed dedicated pools for US/EU/APAC.
[03:10] Ethan Park: That works. I'll need to coordinate with our infra team for IP allowlist and test keys.
[03:15] Priya Shah: Great. I'll send the test plan and a script.
[03:18] Alex Martinez: On pricing — options are: 1) 12-month renewal on hosted with committed tokens (cheapest short-term), 2) Move to dedicated reserved capacity in 1 region now and add regions later, 3) Full 3-region dedicated commit with burst buffer and a 12-month term. Option 3 gives best predictability and a committed discount.
[03:38] Maria Gonzalez: We need predictability, but also want a path that doesn't blow up capex. Can you do phased? Like start with US + EU then add APAC within 90 days?
[03:46] Alex Martinez: Absolutely. We can do a phased approach. Commercially we can price the 3-region commit and also provide a phased amendment that gets prorated credits if you convert later — we'll include that in the quote.
[03:58] Sofia Patel: Will that require new PO each time we add a region?
[04:02] Alex Martinez: We'll make it a single agreement with amendment lines so you can avoid multiple POs if that's preferable. We'll outline both approaches.
[04:10] Ethan Park: Latency targets — we need p95 under 200ms for text generation for EU and APAC. Is that realistic?
[04:18] Priya Shah: With regionally provisioned dedicated pools, p95 under 200ms is achievable for typical sequence lengths. We'll validate in the benchmark — factors are model size, sequence length, and batching. If you push for very large context windows or use 70b+ models there are tradeoffs.
[04:36] Maria Gonzalez: We're on the 30b family mostly, context 2k typical.
[04:40] Priya Shah: That's helpful — simplifies kernel selection.
[04:42] Alex Martinez: On security, we also support VPC peering for Private deployments; Dedicated can have VPC options as well. If you have strict network controls, we can do private connectivity.
[04:54] Ethan Park: For now we prefer dedicated with VPC peering.
[04:58] Priya Shah: Perfect. I'll include network setup steps in the benchmark doc.
[05:03] Maria Gonzalez: A perf question — how does caching behave across regions? If we have requests that come to EU, will a cache miss incur cross-region latency?
[05:12] Priya Shah: Cache is per pool, so if a request lands in EU and it's a miss you'll fetch from model execution in EU; you won't cross-call to US unless routing sends it there. Cross-region KV cache sharing isn't enabled by default — we can discuss a replication model, but it adds complexity and cost.
[05:30] Ethan Park: Okay good. For compliance we also need log retention details and ability to redact PII.
[05:36] Jordan Lee: We have configurable retention and PII redaction options; we'll include specifics in the compliance pack.
[05:44] Sofia Patel: Recap on timeline: we want a quote this week so procurement can review; benchmarking next week or week after, then finalize the PO by mid-May.
[05:54] Alex Martinez: Sounds good — action items we'll put in CRM. I'll send the quote by 2026-04-20. Priya will schedule the benchmark. Jordan will send compliance docs. Ethan will send QPS numbers. Sofia will confirm procurement timeline.
[06:06] Maria Gonzalez: Quick question — alternatives we were evaluating — Anthropic and Bedrock — how do you usually position Redwood vs them for infra?
[06:15] Alex Martinez: Two quick points — first, we focus on predictable inference economics and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Second, our tooling around live cost/latency breakdowns and rollout controls tends to be differentiating for customers who run production at scale. But we'll include a short competitive note in the quote.
[06:32] Priya Shah: Also for private/dedicated the kernel selection and quantization profiles we recommend usually yields lower per-token cost vs generic hosted endpoints, esp for consistent workloads.
[06:44] Ethan Park: Good. On the benchmark — what metrics will you provide? We need p50/p95/p99, token/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens.
[06:54] Priya Shah: Yes, we'll provide those and a breakdown per model variant and config.
[06:58] Alex Martinez: Anything else on open items?
[07:01] Maria Gonzalez: Just a note — if we sign 12 months, we may add a second business unit later; can we anticipate a volume discount if usage grows 2x?
[07:10] Alex Martinez: We can put tiered volume pricing in the agreement. We'll propose a two-tier discount schedule in the quote.
[07:18] Sofia Patel: For procurement we need terms and termination clause length — standard 30 day? Our legal might push for 60.
[07:25] Alex Martinez: We'll put our standard terms and note we can negotiate term language in the enterprise addendum.
[07:31] Ethan Park: One more technical — do you offer per-tenant isolation on logs? We have to ensure logs are separated per sub-org.
[07:39] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can enable tenant-level log scopes and we can push logs to your logging endpoint if needed.
[07:45] Maria Gonzalez: Great.
[07:47] Priya Shah: Ok I'll quickly run through the benchmark plan items after the call — expected inputs: test key, IP allowlist, sample masked payloads, QPS profile, and desired SLOs. We'll need an infra contact.
[07:59] Ethan Park: That's me — I'll be the contact.
[08:02] Alex Martinez: Perfect. We're coming up on time — any final questions?
[08:06] Sofia Patel: None from procurement.
[08:08] Maria Gonzalez: No.
[08:09] Alex Martinez: Ok recap of next steps: Alex to send quote for 3-region dedicated + 12-month extension and phased amendment options; Priya to schedule benchmark and share plan; Jordan to share compliance pack and KMS notes; Ethan to send usage numbers; Sofia to confirm procurement timeline. We'll aim to reconvene after the benchmark to finalize.
[08:30] Alex Martinez: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[08:33] Call ended.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional auto-transcription errors present (names sometimes mis-transcribed, punctuation run-ons). References to shared artifacts are represented as short links in header.
